rows.behavior_contract: Existing PlaintextEnvelope remains the canonical unencrypted auth-key handshake envelope owner. It emits auth_key_id=0:i64, message_id:i64, message_data_length:i32 and four-byte-aligned handshake message data. TcpTransport::exchange_plaintext adds fixed-U-equivalent 0..63 random 32-bit padding words inside outgoing message_data_length. Receive decoding requires zero auth_key_id, a positive four-byte-aligned declared length within the received region, and both declared and total actual post-header length within the existing Fabushi 16 MiB receive budget before body copying. It returns only the declared span: bounded excess tail is ignored, cannot repair a truncated or wrong nonce, and never reaches the TL parser. Reject truncated declaration/body and oversized actual receive regions. Server message-ID semantic validation remains in MessageIdGuard; TL parsing and nonce/state checks remain in AuthKeyHandshake. The source receive rule does not impose the outgoing 252-byte padding cap on extra received tail.
rows.state_machine: AuthKeyHandshake phase emits PlaintextEnvelope -> TcpTransport::exchange_plaintext -> random padded exact unencrypted envelope -> receive/decode exact unencrypted envelope -> MessageIdGuard server-id validation -> existing phase parser/state transition. No connection scheduling or auth-key persistence state is added.

rows.behavior_contract: Fixed-U WebProxy relay frames use an 8-byte header (type, 24-bit big-endian stream id, 32-bit big-endian payload length), a 1 MiB payload ceiling and a 4096-frame batch ceiling. Per-stream flow control starts with 4 MiB send/receive credit; DATA consumes receive/send credit and WINDOW carries one nonzero big-endian u32 credit amount. Receive credit is returned only for bytes actually drained. Browser bootstrap is one-shot/loopback and must complete Hello(0,[1]) -> Welcome(0,empty) before streams open. Carrier replacement/loss fences generations, clears carrier-local state and closes streams. The selected Web carrier is now production-reachable through the existing ProductSettingsOwner -> TelegramClientLease -> RuntimeClient -> telegram-network chain and never falls back to direct TCP.
rows.state_machine: canonical selected Web projection -> prepare one-shot loopback browser bootstrap -> browser auth/MessagePort bridge -> Hello(0,[1]) -> Welcome(0,empty) -> Open logical streams -> bounded Data/Window/Close exchange -> carrier replacement/loss closes all streams and clears generation-local state; the existing RuntimeClient session owner remains authoritative for session invalidation/reconnect.
side_effects: Starts a loopback-only transient browser bootstrap listener inside the existing telegram-network transport owner.
Opens the system browser only through the existing Electron MainEdge shell adapter after strict loopback bootstrap URL validation on settings mutation.
Stream-window state changes only within the selected Web carrier and returns receive credit only after consumer reads.
Carrier replacement/loss closes logical streams and clears Welcome/input/tombstone state without persisting transport state.

rows.behavior_contract: Fixed-U Google/Mozilla DoH responses share a JSON Answer parser that skips malformed entries, optionally filters source-rounded numeric DNS type, preserves accepted data order and defaults missing/non-number TTL to zero. Domain-resolution normalization computes a 10s minimum / 300s maximum effective TTL. Special-config DoH keeps TXT type 16, reproduces QMultiMap ordering by descending QString UTF-16 length with later equal-length insertion first, concatenates and projects QString::toLatin1 bytes. Firestore projects fields.data.stringValue with the same Latin-1 replacement semantics. Structural failures normalize to empty output. Fixed-U ParseHttpDate separately recognizes the source www, dd Mmm yyyy hh:mm:ss GMT shape, validates civil date/time/months and returns UTC time; only the subsequent global unixtime update remains a side effect.
rows.state_machine: carrier response bytes -> pure JSON/field validation -> typed DNS entries or compact special-config bytes -> caller-owned cache/payload decoder; no I/O, timer, proxy, clock, cache mutation or DC/session state
side_effects: No runtime side effects; pure deterministic response transformation only.
Carrier acquisition/scheduling and cache/application side effects remain outside this responsibility.

rows.behavior_contract: A connect/auth-handshake attempt owns and can cancel only its active socket while that attempt is in flight. After successful establishment/adoption, the connect-only deadline and active-stream registration are released without closing the live transport. A later owned RPC temporarily reattaches its request control and clears it when settlement completes. Socket/proxy/read/write/disconnect failures remain typed fail-closed network failures; enabled-proxy failures never fall back to direct transport. RuntimeClient projection change remains the higher-level fence that cancels owned requests and drops live sessions before replacing the transient proxy projection.
rows.state_machine: ProductSettingsOwner/TelegramClientLease projection -> RuntimeClient owned request -> NetworkAttemptControl owns connect/proxy/auth-handshake socket -> success => telegram-network releases connect-only active-stream/deadline ownership while keeping transport alive -> invoke_raw_controlled temporarily attaches the request control for bounded write/flush/read -> clear on settlement -> SessionOwner finish/cancel; projection change => cancel outstanding controls + drop live sessions -> new projection. Fixed-U protocolForFiles socket-buffer tuning remains separately open.
side_effects: Controlled successful establish/resume paths now clear the connect-attempt control before returning the adopted EstablishedSession.

rows.behavior_contract: Continue one explicitly specified repository-development batch from canonical task state without widening scope: resume exclusive checkout-owned active/split state first; freeze the initial selected task ids; establish ownership only through canonical task-state transitions; gate execution on source lineage and safe source preparation; delegate one task performer at a time; route split-required and discovered follow-up work as durable lineage transactions; consolidate only compatible unclaimed unfinished work; preserve recoverable state on races/conflicts; and keep implementation, executable validation, and acceptance distinct. When the explicitly selected scope is the inbox, acquisition is a checkout-bound immutable snapshot transaction; routing preserves project/source lineage, creates only pristine unclaimed implement tasks or receipt-only dispositions, resolves retired alias/split history to live successors, and publishes only explicit task/project/receipt paths before digest-checked finalization. Supplied-video intake is a subordinate evidence transformation: bind the local source by digest/probe metadata, use decoded presentation timestamps as timing authority, derive only validated frame/crop/sheet evidence, keep original video and bulk extraction untracked, hand later performers only durable task inputs, and fail closed on missing tools, malformed selection, empty/non-deterministic decode, count mismatch, or incomplete target output. The concrete workspace helper binds execution to one checkout tag and canonical repository, isolates slot/inbox/routing/health worktrees, seals inbox transactions by content digest, gates Start/Retry on canonical task and source-lineage state, keeps base/green/run refs as local recovery metadata, publishes only explicit paths through refreshed/rebased semantic validation, and finalizes or aborts without discarding changed live input or unsafe recovery state. The fixed-U workspace regression suite independently pins checkout/worktree isolation, narrow transaction publication/finalize semantics, atomic task Start/Retry plus source-lineage recovery, owned-path source commits, batch race handling and approval-ref recovery; it explicitly does not provide a direct abort-command or digest-algorithm unit case, so those remain separately authored Fabushi obligations.

Pending split/consolidation/routing markers are durable recovery boundaries; no-repeat completion markers prevent duplicate transactions. rows.concurrency_and_cancellation: Start/finish/split/routing/consolidation publication uses one-owner/CAS semantics. Concurrent claim wins are resolved by refresh without stealing. Pre-commit consolidation races write nothing; unsafe committed publication state is preserved. Interruption leaves task-local state resumable and does not manufacture a Block. Inbox publication is isolated from the task slot, rejects unsafe/unpublished canonical state for new acquisition, retries only ordinary non-fast-forward races after refresh/rebase, and preserves semantic-conflict/remote-failure state without force publication. Workspace-helper publication reruns semantic validation after rebase, retries only ordinary non-fast-forward/fetch-first races, preserves unpublished work on semantic/rebase/remote failure, and never treats a private recovery mirror as canonical authority.

rows.behavior_contract: Perform one explicitly requested, intent-aware Git rebase only in the current checkout: resolve the exact ONTO/REPLAY_BASE/OLD_TIP lineage and replay set before mutation; refuse dirty, ambiguous, sibling-worktree-owned or stale-target states that require a decision; keep task/process queues out of branch integration; resolve conflicts by reconstructing both sides' intent rather than mechanically selecting ours/theirs; review rerere and empty-commit cases explicitly; preserve reflog-based recovery and unknown in-progress state; verify the entire replay semantically with range-diff/log/status; and keep publication outside the rebase owner so no push or force-push occurs.
rows.state_machine: explicit request -> resolve branch/ONTO/REPLAY_BASE/OLD_TIP -> preflight current worktree/dirty/in-progress/remote snapshot -> explicit merge-history decision if needed -> non-interactive rebase -> per-conflict mechanical or intent-history resolution | genuine contradiction question -> continue/resume | explicit abort/recovery -> whole-series semantic range-diff/log/status -> report undo/conflicts/skips/uncertainty/publication need without push
side_effects: Mutates only the explicitly selected current Git worktree/branch through the requested rebase.
Creates no ai-task records, backup branches/tags, shipping runtime state, product task state or platform-core state.
Does not fetch without explicit approval and does not push or force-push.
failure_cases: A branch checked out in a sibling worktree is rebased from the current checkout
Dirty work is silently stashed/reset instead of stopping for a decision
A literal proposed command is executed although its resolved replay list contradicts the user's prose
A remote-tracking target is silently fetched or treated as fresh without its snapshot identity being disclosed
A new rebase is started while another rebase is already in progress
Merge commits are flattened or preserved without the explicit requested/default decision boundary
Conflict stages are oriented backwards so replayed work is silently reverted
Overlapping logic is resolved by ours/theirs, marker deletion or hard-conflict skip rather than intent history
Upstream-deleted structure is resurrected merely to host the old patch
A genuine semantic contradiction is guessed instead of surfaced for a decision
A rerere resolution is accepted without reviewing both intents and the staged result
An empty commit is skipped without proving its intended end state is already present
Unknown resume state is auto-aborted or destructively reset
Backup branches/tags are created despite reflog being the declared undo authority
Whole-series range-diff changed/disappeared mappings are ignored
Git command success is promoted to build/test/acceptance evidence
The rebase owner pushes or force-pushes rewritten history
Branch integration is routed into continue/perform-task/process-inbox or shipping Product Tasks/Automations

rows.behavior_contract: Bounded source-informed Human direct-message admission and settlement in the existing Fabushi Session/Transcript owner. Before resource access, transcript mutation, acknowledgement settlement or overlap use, a returned row must match the authenticated local/selected-peer pair. Only a local-authored request nonce may settle its local intent; canonical-ID and nonce lookup both preserve immutable sender, text, dispatched reply and resource identities. Peer request provenance remains separate. Independent deterministic rejections may coexist with valid progress, but retryable resource/storage failure stops ordered replay. These selected target security and durability rules are not a claim of identical Telegram API semantics or full history/reaction parity. NMR-18/19/20 additionally admit only direct-pair reaction summaries (0,false), (1,false), (1,true), (2,true), reject duplicate exact emoji strings, and project at most one local and one peer actor per item. Incoming message validation precedes peer early-return, overlap and resource access; reaction POST validation precedes legacy nonce changes, durable writes and publication.
rows.state_machine: The current qualified Session/Transcript route persists pending intent/resources before dispatch, admits acknowledgements into the same durable row and projects entries-upserted. afterId/historyCursor coverage advances only after admitted/materialized monotonic pages; known IDs do not end gap traversal. ReadAt merges by RFC3339 instant and desired-active reaction intent survives ambiguous POST/restart. Existing forwarding now journals whole immutable batches with expected-value CAS and typed source-denial recovery; exact59 Human38/sharebox1/journal3 exercise these bounded paths. Native CLI/gateway remain direct existing Host consumers; NMR-CLI-HOST-01 restores their native feature selection rather than adding another owner.
